issues.title: Adopt CIMD multi-method client authentication (CIMD PR #99)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
oauth-wg/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document#99 (for #87 and #92) would let a Client ID Metadata Document declare several client authentication methods through `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported` (OpenID Connect RP Metadata Choices), and would have a server assume `none` when a document declares neither member. #39 made the core's sender-constraint rule accept any declared method. These still depend on the single `token_endpoint_auth_method` member:

- [ ] Core 5.4.1: the public-client condition ("declares `token_endpoint_auth_method` of `none`"). PR #99's own example combines `none`, `jwks_uri`, and a `private_key_jwt` choice. Define it by the method CIMD determines.
- [ ] Core 5.4 and 8.2: the rejection of a document that omits `token_endpoint_auth_method`, and whether a document carrying only `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported` satisfies the explicit-declaration requirement.
- [ ] Registration 3 and 6: the rejection of `none` and of an omitted method.
- [ ] After CIMD -03: check again the core's citations of CIMD Sections 4.3 and 8.7. PR #99 adds a top-level section, so they may renumber.

Raised in the reviews of #39.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
From the pre-publication cold read of 2026-10-28 (deferred to -01):
- [ ] A document declaring token_endpoint_auth_method none but carrying jwks, presented with a DPoP proof at the token endpoint, is bound under one rule in core 5.2 and review-only under another; core 5.2, 5.4.1, and 8.2 key the token-endpoint rule on different conditions (public client versus no key material).

issues.title: Make error codes consistent across presentation, refresh, and registration
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Points where the error code is inconsistent or missing:

- [ ] A digest mismatch is `invalid_client` at presentation (core 5.5, 8.2) but `statement_required` at refresh (core 8.3). The remedy is the same: a statement over the current document.
- [ ] Reaching the bound on establishments returns `invalid_client` (core 5.5, 8.2), which RFC 6749 uses for authentication failure, yet core 5.5 says the statement and proof are sound and invites a retry.
- [ ] A statement under a registration that is not statement-governed: core 5.1 rejects a `software_statement` parameter in any other role with `invalid_request`, while registration 4 says the statement "neither renews nor alters" the registration. Registration 4 also sends a statement from an unaccepted issuer to registration Section 6, which covers only registration endpoints.
- [ ] Core 5.1.1 forbids `software_statement` in an authorization request, but core 8.4 gives no error code for it.
- [ ] Registration 3 requires the document's `client_id` member to match the statement's `sub`, but registration 6 gives no code for a mismatch.

From the pre-publication review (#38).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
From the pre-publication cold read of 2026-10-28 (deferred to -01):
- [ ] At refresh, the proven-key check and a replacement's document checks can fail on the same document with different codes (invalid_grant versus statement_required). Consider fixing the order: proven-key check first, its failures invalid_grant.
- [ ] Retrieval failures other than timeouts and 5xx (404, a non-JSON body, a document failing CIMD validation) have no assigned code at presentation or registration; temporarily_unavailable invites endless retries.
- [ ] invalid_client, which signals a credential failure, is used for a retryable establishment bound (core 8.2, 12.3).
- [ ] Core 3.2 checks neither that kid is present nor that alg is one the trust configuration accepts for the issuer.

issues.title: Bind statements pulled at the pushed authorization request endpoint
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Core 5.2 lets a server pull statements "when it resolves the document of a client that presented no statement", which includes a pushed authorization request. The binding list covers only the token endpoint and the authorization endpoint.

- [ ] Say how a statement pulled at the pushed authorization request endpoint binds: as at the token endpoint for a confidential client, and under 5.4.1 for a public client.
- [ ] Core 5.6: an establishment from a statement pulled at the authorization endpoint has no proven key until code redemption, yet redemption "MUST demonstrate possession of the same proven key". State that the key bound at redemption becomes the proven key.

From the pre-publication review (#38).

issues.title: Withdrawal checks at new admission and for registrations without the validity model
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
- [ ] Core 3.2: a server must reject a statement it holds a refusal record for, but only refresh (core 5.6.1) and token requests under a statement-governed registration (registration 3.1) say a server SHOULD consult its withdrawal mechanism. Decide whether a server that uses a mechanism should also consult it before a new admission.
- [ ] Core 4 says a required issuer exists so that withholding the statement cannot restore access a customer withdrew. A server that does not apply the registration validity model keeps a registration after the required issuer's statement expires or is withdrawn. State whether the required-issuer rule reaches such registrations.

From the pre-publication review (#38).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
From the pre-publication cold read of 2026-10-28 (deferred to -01):
- [ ] A required issuer (core Section 4) governs only new admission. Grants opened before the requirement was configured, or under a required-issuer statement that stopped being renewed, keep refreshing. Registration already applies the requirement to every request; consider a matching refresh rule in core 5.6.1 (reject unless the recorded statement or a replacement is a current statement from the required issuer).

issues.title: Key rotation on refresh and inline jwks
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
- [ ] Core 5.6.1: "Refresh never rotates the establishment's key." A confidential client that rotates keys at its `jwks_uri` loses every grant once the proven key leaves the document. Consider accepting, outside 5.4.1, any key the current reviewed document carries.
- [ ] oauth-wg/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document#61 proposes discouraging inline `jwks` in a Client ID Metadata Document. Core 12.1 advises issuers to attest `jwks` inline so the digest covers the keys. If CIMD discourages `jwks`, that advice runs against the base specification.
- [ ] Related CIMD discussion on treating key changes as normal: #57 and #11 there.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body: From an external review (2026-10-28): define two recovery paths rather than a universal rollover. Continuity-preserving rotation, where both old and new proof material are available and an explicitly authorized migration proves possession of both, is valuable but can be standardized separately. Continuity-breaking recovery, where the old key is lost or compromised, is the baseline core already states ("Refresh never rotates the establishment's key. A client that needs a new key performs a new presentation."); the draft should also state its consequences: a new grant, and possibly new user consent.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
From the pre-publication cold read of 2026-10-28 (deferred to -01):
- [ ] Core bounds reuse of a client's key set and held document octets, but not of an issuer's statement key set, so how long a removed issuer key continues to verify after compromise is left to each implementation.

issues.title: Registration endpoint at servers that implement only the core
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
A server that implements the core but not the registration draft, and whose RFC 7591 endpoint verifies software statements through a generic path, could accept a statement of this profile at registration and take client metadata from the request. #38 restricted statement keys to statements of this profile and narrowed core 12.2 to state the remaining exposure.

- [ ] Decide whether to add: "An authorization server that does not implement [REGISTRATION] MUST reject a statement of this profile in a registration request." It was proposed in the review and left out of #38.

issues.title: Record and enforce the tenant of a statement-governed registration
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Core 5.6 records the tenant in an establishment. Registration 3.1 records the governing statement's identity but not the tenant, and nothing confines a registered client to the tenant its statement's `aud_tenant` names. At a multi-tenant server with one registration endpoint, a statement for tenant A could yield a `client_id` usable in tenant B, the confusion core 12.4 describes.

- [ ] Add the tenant to the record in registration 3.1, if the server hosts more than one.
- [ ] Reject a request under the registration in another tenant, and choose the error code.

From the pre-publication review (#38).

issues.title: Copied statements at registration: default and published statements
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
- [ ] Registration 5: "The safe default is one registration per (`iss`, `sub`)". Under a reject policy, the first holder of a copy locks the publisher out (registration 9.1). An idempotent response returns no credentials, and the client authenticates with a key from the document, so the publisher can still use it. Consider making the idempotent response the default.
- [ ] Core 13 notes published statements are readable by anyone, so a published statement whose `statement_uses` permits registration is a public bearer artifact. Consider "A client SHOULD NOT publish a statement whose `statement_uses` permits registration" in core 5.2.

From the pre-publication review (#38).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
From the pre-publication cold read of 2026-10-28 (deferred to -01):
- [ ] Registration should state that a statement consumed at registration must list registration in statement_uses; a reader learns it only from the unapproved_software_statement definition.
- [ ] A registration created from a statement not confined to a tenant is checked against core 3.2's tenant-scoped requirement only in the tenant where it registers; nothing applies that requirement again in another tenant.
- [ ] If the server registers the client with its CIMD URL as client_id, a token request carrying a statement is both a runtime presentation and a delivery, with different rules.

issues.title: Repeated-consumption edge cases: equal iat and bound exhaustion
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
- [ ] Core 6 rejects a statement whose `iat` is earlier than the retained `iat`. Two statements with the same `iat` both pass, and the issuer's MUST that `iat` increase strictly (core 3) is not observable by the server. Consider also rejecting a statement with an equal `iat` and a different `jti`.
- [ ] One party with many accounts can exhaust the per-(`iss`, `sub`) bound for software admitted under 5.4.1, after which every new installation gets `invalid_client`. The per-resource-owner bound assumes one account per user.

From the pre-publication review (#38).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body: From an external review (2026-10-28): the reviewer read the iat rule as global ordering with avoidable coordination, and suggested a separate revision claim or a narrower guarantee. Assessment: the floor is already narrow (each trusting server keeps it per iss, sub, and tenant, from statements it has itself accepted), and a revision claim needs the same issuer-side coordination (core 12.5). Worth doing for -01: state in Security Considerations the attack the floor stops (a client holding a superseded, broader statement delaying a narrowing without any withdrawal mechanism) and what expiry, withdrawal, and the digest already cover. The equal-iat case above remains open.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
From the pre-publication cold read of 2026-10-28 (deferred to -01):
- [ ] Core 5.6.1's replacement requirements omit the iat floor, which only Section 6 states.
- [ ] Core 5.6.1 does not say what a server does with a newer statement offered on refresh while the recorded one is still current, or whether a pulled establishment accepts a presented replacement (registration renews on any delivery).
- [ ] Registration 3.1 leaves three repeated public-client registration cases undefined: a statement with a different iss, a tenant-confined statement against an unrestricted registration, and the governing statement itself after another instance raised the floor.

issues.title: Minimum document size servers accept
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Core 3.1 makes a response over the server's configured size bound a retrieval failure, and sets no floor. CIMD Section 8.7 recommends a 5 KB read limit as a SHOULD, so a statement over a larger document works at some servers and not others.

- [ ] Consider: "An issuer SHOULD NOT issue a statement over a document larger than 5 KB, and a trusting authorization server SHOULD accept documents up to that size." Align with CIMD if it changes the recommendation.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
From the pre-publication cold read of 2026-10-28 (deferred to -01):
- [ ] No rule tells an issuer to refuse to sign a document with duplicate member names, or one whose client_id member differs from sub; servers reject such documents, so those statements can never be used.

issues.title: Issuer key discovery without RFC 8414 metadata
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Core 2 defines the Issuer as "The authorization server that signs a software statement", and core 4 discovers its statement keys only from `software_statement_jwks_uri` in its RFC 8414 metadata. A marketplace reviewer that is not otherwise an authorization server must publish authorization server metadata to issue statements.

- [ ] Decide whether a trusting authorization server may configure an issuer's statement key-set URL directly, and what that does to the key-separation argument of core 12.2.

issues.title: Editorial pass for -01
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
- [ ] Terminology: "watermark" (core 4.1, 5.2, 5.4.1, 6) versus "`iat` floor" (core 5.3, 5.6.1, 8.1; registration 4, 6); issuer versus "reviewer" (core 4.1) versus "review authority" (core 7.1); "identifier scope" (core 3.2) versus "client identifier namespaces" (core 4); the three senses of "tenant" (the server's tenant, the issuer's customer in 4.1, the client's customers in 12.4); "Consumer" in the title of 12.4.
- [ ] Terms used but not defined in the core: "current", "review-only", "delivery" (defined only in the registration draft).
- [ ] Core 5.4: "Two rejections still apply to such a document" follows "the requirements above do not apply". Rewrite.
- [ ] Registration 3.2: the 70-word sentence beginning "A client offers one in an ordinary" update request. Split it.
- [ ] Core 4.1: "tenants of a reviewer" means the issuer's customers, not `aud_tenant` tenants. Reword.
- [ ] Core 9: add a decoded statement (JOSE header and claims).
- [ ] Core 12.5: move the normative text (the URL-policy MUST, the SHOULD list, "MUST NOT fall back") into Section 5, which cites it.
- [ ] Core 5.1: "A request that asks an authorization server to issue a software statement" refers to a request no submitted document defines. Delete it or mark it as defined elsewhere.
- [ ] Core 5.1: "REQUIRED for presentation", although pulled statements are also presentation. Say "REQUIRED to present a statement in a request."
- [ ] Core 1: "an authorization server it has never dealt with" overstates, since core 4 requires out-of-band issuer configuration.
- [ ] Place the replacement MUSTs the same way in core 5.6.1 (one per item) and registration 3.2 (one in the lead-in).
- [ ] Expand "CIMD" in both titles. Cite RFC 7515 Section 2 for base64url without padding and RFC 8259 Section 4 for duplicate member names.

From the pre-publication review (#38).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
From the pre-publication cold read of 2026-10-28 (deferred to -01):
- [ ] Registration cites [STATEMENT] about 40 times without section numbers; add them once both are posted.
- [ ] [OPENID-FED] renders n.d. with no authors.
- [ ] Add a decoded statement (header and payload) example to core Section 9.
- [ ] Core Acknowledgments refers to an issuance draft not yet on the datatracker.
- [ ] Abstract says portable 'across the authorization servers that trust its issuer', Introduction says 'in the statement's audience'; and 'bytes' versus 'octets'.
- [ ] One concept, several names: 'identifier scope', 'issuer's scope', and 'client identifier namespaces'; 'digested document' and 'reviewed document'.
- [ ] Core 14.1 table: the document match is as last retrieved within the reuse period (5.5); 14.7's proven-key-gone case does not apply to 5.4.1 grants.
- [ ] IANA usage-location names ('token error response', 'client registration error response') differ from the registry's ('token endpoint', 'registration endpoint').

issues.title: Deferred keyword decisions
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Keyword changes considered in the normative pass and left for a decision:

- [ ] Registration 9.3: restore SHOULD for the lowercase "should prefer those from a reviewed document".
- [ ] Core 4: keep or lowercase the namespace-constraint SHOULD ("Trust configuration SHOULD constrain each issuer to the client identifier namespaces it is expected to attest").
- [ ] Core 10: keep or lowercase the certificate MUST ("a trusting authorization server MUST validate the server's certificate"), which restates TLS practice.
- [ ] Core 12.5: keep or lowercase the URL-policy MUST ("the authorization server MUST apply its URL, redirect, address-range, transport, and content-type policy").

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body: Decided before -00: keep all four as they are. The namespace-scoping SHOULD (core 4), the certificate-validation MUST (core 10), and the independent URL-policy MUST (core 12.5) stay; the branding preference in registration 9.3 stays lowercase. Restating a security requirement is not by itself a reason to weaken it.

issues.title: Update references after -00 is posted
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Once both drafts are on the datatracker:

- [ ] Switch [STATEMENT] in the registration draft and [REGISTRATION] in the core from datatracker URLs to `I-D.mcguinness-oauth-cimd-sw-stmt` and `I-D.mcguinness-oauth-cimd-sw-stmt-registration`, so they render with a date and revision.
- [ ] Add the author and date to [OPENID-FED].

issues.title: Questions to expect from the working group
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Not defects; positions to prepare before the drafts are discussed:

- [ ] Generic names with profile-only meaning: `software_statement_jwks_uri`, `software-statement+jwt`, the `software_statement` parameter. Expect a request for a `cimd-` prefix.
- [ ] No registry for `statement_uses` values.
- [ ] A normative reference to ID-JAG for one optional claim (`aud_tenant`).
- [ ] RFC 7592 is Experimental: registration places requirements on RFC 7592 update requests while citing it informatively. A normative reference would need a downref call.
- [ ] Why a digest over raw octets rather than JCS (RFC 8785).
- [ ] `tls_client_auth` (RFC 8705) cannot present, because the proven key must be in the document's `jwks` or at its `jwks_uri`.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Further positions from an external review (2026-10-28):
- Terminology: 'reviewed software' versus 'reviewed client metadata'. Core keeps the policy term and states the limit in Security Considerations (What a Statement Attests, with a table of what admission establishes).
- Layering: the reviewer sees three layers in core (portable validation, OAuth admission, continuing authorization) and would keep the third minimal. Expect a request to split or shrink establishment and refresh rules.
- Review meaning: a malware scan and an enterprise audit produce the same statement. Position: issuer-scoped local trust policy in core; a review-policy identifier only as a later extension.
- Registration renewal scope, and RFC 7592's Experimental status for the update-request path (already noted above).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
From the pre-publication cold read of 2026-10-28 (deferred to -01):
- [ ] [IDJAG] is normative only for the optional aud_tenant claim name, which core restates; expect a request to make it informative (and RFC 9700, used only to explain, likewise).
- [ ] draft-ietf-oauth-rfc7523bis updates RFC 7523; expect a request to cite it.
- [ ] Core 5.1 does not require the client_id parameter when the client authenticates with private_key_jwt, which RFC 7523 makes optional.
- [ ] Core 14.3's key separation 'guards against' generic servers for an authorization-server issuer but, for an issuer with a recorded key set, only limits the exposure.

issues.title: Coordinate with the CIMD draft
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Comments and issues to raise in oauth-wg/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document, each offering resolution options:

- [ ] #61 (inline `jwks`): the use case for keeping inline `jwks` is digest-bound keys for software statements.
- [ ] #92 and PR #99 (omitted or multiple authentication methods): put this profile's explicit-declaration requirement on record before CIMD -03.
- [ ] #91 and PR #97 (consistent documents): a digest over the retrieved octets is a technical check of the consistency #91 asks for.
- [ ] New issue on CIMD Section 4.3: it invites carrying `software_statement` inside the document, but a statement there cannot bind the document's own bytes. Options: Section 4.3 notes the limit and points to carrying statements outside the document, or it stays generic and this profile carries the caveat.
- [ ] Watch PR #63 (`Accept: application/cimd+json`) and #77 (negative caching). #39 made the core defer to CIMD on both.

issues.title: Issuance and status cleanups
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
For the issuance and status drafts, which are not being submitted yet:

- [ ] Terms imported from the core: Metadata Digest and Effective Expiry; "issuer trust configuration" in the status draft; the clash between the core's Establishment and the issuance draft's use of the word; SSF term casing.
- [ ] Issuance: the pointer to redemption, and the reason given for the callback in the design rationale.
- [ ] Status: "defines two".
- [ ] Status: duplicate detection per issuer, checked against RFC 8417.

issues.title: Issuance: keep or defer the software-statement redirect flow
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
A simplification review suggested deferring the software-statement authorization flow in the issuance draft, unless browser bootstrap is an immediate requirement.

## What the flow adds

- the `software_statement_code` response type and its code lifecycle;
- the `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:software-statement` redemption;
- the associated authorization-response security rules.

All of this sits alongside the token exchange profile.

## Option A: keep it

It is the only path in the draft for a client that has no initial credential to obtain a statement through a browser interaction. Token exchange does not cover that case.

## Option B: defer it

A first issuance profile would cover token exchange, renewal, and asynchronous review, with initial credentials provisioned separately. That removes a substantial protocol surface, but loses integrated browser bootstrap.

## Decision needed

Is browser bootstrap for a client with no initial credential a launch requirement? For example, the MCP profile sketch (`sketches/mcp-profile-sketch.md`) and the deployment model.

The issuance draft is not going to -00 now, so this does not block the core and registration submissions.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body: From an external review (2026-10-28): make token exchange the first interoperable issuance path where a bootstrap credential exists, and decide later whether browser-based issuance needs standardizing. Also: returning the statement in access_token with token_type N_A needs negative test cases showing a generic client or resource server does not treat it as a Bearer token (the draft already forbids that use).

issues.title: Status: freshness profile and durable status state
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From an external review (2026-10-28), for the status draft before its -00:
- [ ] Implementers may read status support as immediate revocation. Consider a profile for deployments requiring continuous review: a maximum accepted status age and fail-closed behavior when it is exceeded, leaving other deployments free to choose availability.
- [ ] The rule against replacing a held Status List Token with one whose iat is earlier protects only while the server keeps that token. State what happens after a restart or state loss, and whether durable state is expected.
- [ ] Core now allows an issuer that is not an authorization server, with a configured statement key set (#50). Status still takes Status List Token keys from the issuer's authorization server metadata and separates SET keys from software_statement_jwks_uri. Decide whether status requires an authorization server issuer or accepts configured key sets too.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body: Specifics from checking the core change for #50: status takes Status List Token keys only from the jwks_uri in the issuer's RFC 8414 metadata (status 3.2, Event Issuer Trust and Keys), and the SET location rule names only software_statement_jwks_uri. An issuer that is not an authorization server therefore has no withdrawal mechanism in the family yet, and 'a trusting authorization server can resolve those statuses for any issuer it has configured' overclaims. Options: a status key-set URL recorded in trust configuration and kept apart from the statement key set, and adding the recorded statement key-set URL to the SET location rule.

issues.title: MCP profile: attested native clients need DPoP-bound access tokens
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body: From an external review (2026-10-28): the attested-keys draft issues DPoP-bound access tokens and cannot be used with a resource server that does not accept them, while the MCP profile issues Bearer access tokens as MCP requires. An attested native MCP client therefore gets the stronger end-to-end guarantee only where the MCP server accepts DPoP. The MCP profile should say so, and distinguish hosted confidential clients, hosted public clients, and native clients, with native software needing additional evidence for assurance about the running application.

issues.title: Conformance suite and implementer guide
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From an external review (2026-10-28), after -00:
- [ ] Shared test vectors and protocol tests: exact-byte digest mismatches, replay and rollback, duplicate JSON members, unauthorized issuers, metadata changes, stale status, grant continuation after expiry, missing or replaced proof keys, and downgrade from reviewed to unreviewed admission.
- [ ] A cross-draft capability matrix (the FAQ now has a first version: what each draft guarantees over the life of a grant).
- [ ] An implementer guide outside the drafts for deterministic serialization of documents, coordinating publication with issuance, retaining earlier approved document versions, CDN behavior, and rollout.

pulls.title: Review round 2026-10-06: consistency fixes across all three drafts
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
A review round across all three drafts. The review used two cold working-group reviewers (one for the statement draft, one for issuance and signals), a cold implementer walking four roles, three reference verifiers, and a full read of the rendered text. Every finding was checked against the draft text before being applied. There is one commit per finding, so any of them can be dropped on its own.

The branch also carries two commits made earlier to `main` and not yet pushed: babedf0 (what `aud_tenant` does not bind) and 6535b77 (showing and bounding the tenant an approval confines a statement to).

## High

1. **Expired registration had three error answers.**
   - Before: §5.1 and §5.2 gave `unauthorized_client` at the authorization and PAR endpoints, while §6.6 and §10 gave `invalid_client` "at every endpoint".
   - Now: `invalid_client` at the token and PAR endpoints, and `statement_required` at the authorization endpoint. §10 already reasons that a client should learn it needs a statement, and the recovery path is the same (deliver a replacement through PAR).
2. **Expired statement at presentation.** Table 1 gave `invalid_client` but the §10 prose gave `statement_required`. It is now `statement_required`.
3. **Replacement delivery.** §5.2 re-derives a registration's metadata from the replacement, while §6.6 said a delivery "does not otherwise alter the registration". §6.6 now follows §5.2.
4. **Default audience.**
   - Before: statement §3 told issuers to name an audience, issuance Privacy told them to restrict it only where they mean to limit reach, and issuance §5 forbade adding an audience the client didn't request.
   - Now: an issuer can require an audience, rejecting a request without one with `invalid_target` (RFC 8707 covers a missing target). On renewal, the prior `aud` is both the default and the ceiling.
5. **`iat` watermark at a multi-tenant consumer.** It is now kept per consumer tenant, so statements an issuer makes for different tenants don't supersede each other.
6. **Per-instance registration.** §7 said software whose instances hold their own keys "registers per instance", which §5's document-only rule forbids. That case now points to the endorsement extension.
7. **DPoP nonce.** A `use_dpop_nonce` challenge no longer consumes the software statement code. Before, any server requiring nonces broke public-client issuance.
8. **Key compartments.**
   - A consumer accepts any key in the issuer's JWK Set for statements. A key there that signs the status list or events can therefore also sign statements; both drafts now say so.
   - Signals now verifies events with keys from the SSF Transmitter configuration. That location must differ from the issuer's own, and a receiver can check this.

## Medium and low

- **Statement:**
  - Tenant and status claims are now recorded with what the statement governs.
  - SUSPENDED status now follows configured policy everywhere.
  - The presentation order is stated as processing performs it.
  - A runtime digest mismatch now has defined behavior.
  - Public clients are no longer promised a document key.
  - The deployment model now says which decision a request carries when two issuers govern a client.
  - Missing error codes are named, and replacements get the same audience rule everywhere.
  - Editorial fixes: the definitions list, the table header, and several cross-references.
- **Issuance:**
  - Renewal is listed among the ways to obtain a replacement, and it keeps `tenant` and `aud_tenant`.
  - The snapshot is re-bound on any digest change.
  - The polling example now uses `private_key_jwt` with a URL `client_id`.
  - Who can cancel a deferral by replaying its code is bounded.
  - The initial access token binding rules now agree.
  - DPoP is required at redemption wherever `dpop_jkt` was sent.
  - Each request failure has a named error.
  - A registry change that DTR already requests is dropped.
- **Signals:**
  - An event is never grounds for refusal; receivers fetch afresh and keep the copy they hold until that succeeds.
  - A transmitter sends an event only once the changed list is retrievable.
  - Streams are scoped by `aud`.
  - `event_timestamp` and Status List terms are described accurately.

## Normative changes to look at

- **Deliberately removed:**
  - The registration grace-period MAY (§5.2 restoration replaces it).
  - §6.4's MAY to accept a changed document or narrow the policy, folded into a single local-policy permission.
  - The signals MAY to refuse while a fetch is pending.
  - The signals MAY to put event keys in the issuer's key set.
- **Design change:** the source of event signing keys in signals.
- **Added:**
  - A MUST to verify the initial access token's key binding.
  - A nonce challenge doesn't consume the code.
  - A transmitter MUST NOT send an event before the list is retrievable.
  - A MAY to limit replay revocation to replays that pass PKCE.

## Not applied

- **PUSHED-DCR** has expired; it is left as an informative reference.
- **An example event** wasn't added: its type URN plus indentation exceeds the 72-column figure limit.
- **Deferred:** a normative audit of requirements no other party can observe, a terminology pass, and DTR's status as an individual draft and normative dependency.
- **Open tension:** §5.3 still calls a runtime digest mismatch "a policy input rather than an automatic failure". The new §6.4 is consistent with that reading, but a reader may stumble on it.

## Checks

- All three drafts build after every commit.
- idnits warnings are identical to the pre-round versions.
- The before-and-after BCP 14 sentence diff shows only the changes listed above.
- Dependency claims were verified against CIMD-02, DTR-00, Token Status List-21, IDJAG-04, OIDC Enterprise, SSF 1.0, CAEP, and the RFC sections cited. IANA entries were checked against the live registries.

pulls.title: Critique round 2026-10-07: statement key set, consumption limits, review-only loopback, MCP sketch
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
This PR applies a design critique of all three drafts. It is a substance review, not the consistency round in #1. Three cold critics read the drafts:
- a skeptical working-group participant, arguing necessity and shape against CIMD, ABCA, approval-based DCR and OpenID Federation, using their current text;
- an OAuth security reviewer, who built a threat model and ranked attacks;
- the operator of an MCP authorization server, grounded in the MCP 2026-07-28 authorization spec and CIMD-02.

Their load-bearing claims were checked against the drafts, and the MCP and Enterprise-Managed Authorization facts against the live specs. There is one commit per finding.

## Decisions taken

- **Registration stays in the statement draft**, with targeted fixes. The alternative was to move registration consumption and the validity model together into a companion draft. They can't be separated: the validity model is the fix for registrations that outlive their review.
- **Loopback public clients get review-only presentation** rather than refusal.
- **The `iat` watermark stays**, with guidance that instances share one current statement.

## Changes

### Statement draft

- **Separate statement key set.**
  - New AS metadata `software_statement_jwks_uri` holds statement signing keys only.
  - Consumers verify statements against it, and status lists against `jwks_uri`.
  - This closes the downgrade at RFC 7591 servers that don't implement the profile; a new "Servers That Do Not Implement This Specification" section explains it.
  - It also means a status-list key can no longer sign statements.
- **`consumable_at` claim.** An issuer can limit a statement to `presentation` or `registration`. The name is a placeholder.
- **Registration rule.** Registration refuses a keyless (`none`) document with a non-https redirect URI. Registration has no review-only form, because the registration is the admission.
- **Review-only presentation.** A document with loopback or private-use redirects is presented review-only:
  - it creates no establishment and admits nothing an unreviewed client wouldn't get;
  - it never satisfies a "reviewed software" policy;
  - it doesn't advance the watermark.
- **No credentials on repeat registration.** An idempotent registration response never returns the registration's credentials.
- **Withdrawal ends refresh.** A refusal record now ends refresh-based continuation regardless of local policy.
- **Establishment bound.** Only establishments whose grant completed count toward the per-software bound. Before, anyone holding a copy of a public statement could lock legitimate installations out.
- **Status rollback.** A server refuses an older Status List Token in place of a newer one.
- **Retained documents.** Retained document octets are revalidated on the document's caching schedule.
- **Customer's issuer.** A customer's own issuer is required in that customer's tenant, so a holder can't present a broader listing to evade its withdrawal.
- **Shared statements.** Watermark guidance says instances obtain the current statement from a shared source.

### Issuance draft

- **Changed document on renewal.** Renewal over a changed document gets the decision a first issuance gets, so a compromise of the client's origin can't be laundered through renewal.
- **Corrected claim.** The claim about what renewal binding protects against was false for `jwks_uri` documents; it's now accurate.
- **Status lists.** They are signed only with `jwks_uri` keys, never statement keys, and always carry `exp`.
- **Withdrawing superseded statements.** An issuer withdraws a statement whose replacement removed a key, redirect URI or scope.
- **Approval screen.** It shows the client's origin as its identity and marks display metadata as client-asserted. An issuer limits approvers to enrolled publisher namespaces.
- **DTR reference.** It now points to `draft-ietf-oauth-deferred-token-response`, the working-group adoption that replaced the Gerber draft on 2026-09-23.

### Signals draft

- **Key location.** The Transmitter configuration's `jwks_uri` must differ from the statement key set rather than from `jwks_uri`.

### Repository

- **README.** It points at the working-group DTR draft.
- **New sketch.** `mcp-profile-sketch.md` is new and non-normative. It covers a server pulling the review (from a location the document names, or from the issuer) instead of the client carrying it, an outline of an MCP profile, and how the statement composes with MCP Enterprise-Managed Authorization.

## Normative changes to look at

- **Replaced on purpose:**
  - §6.3.1's rejection of loopback documents, replaced by review-only presentation;
  - the §6.5.1 refusal-record sentence, now stronger;
  - the status-list key source, in both the statement and issuance drafts;
  - the signals key-location rule, now aimed at the statement key set.
- **Reworded:** every other removed BCP 14 sentence.
- **Added:** about twenty requirements, listed above.

## Not applied

- **Stronger renewal fix (D4):** pinning key thumbprints at issuance, or reversing the issuance draft's SHOULD that prefers `jwks_uri`.
- **Canonical or partial-review digest.**
- **Trimming issuance:** cutting it down to token exchange first, with the redirect flow and DTR second.
- **For the author:** the embedded-statement disagreement with CIMD §4.3, and the document-located reference, both go to the CIMD editors.

## Checks

- **Builds:** all three drafts build after every commit.
- **idnits:** warnings unchanged, except one fewer "outdated draft" in issuance now that DTR points at the WG draft.
- **BCP 14 diff:** the before-and-after sentence diff shows only the changes listed above.

pulls.title: Draft the MCP Reviewed Client Software profile, with pulled statements
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
This PR drafts an MCP profile of the family and defines the server-pull mechanism the profile needs. The pull mechanism is defined normatively in the statement draft.

## MCP profile

`mcp/reviewed-client-software.mdx`, titled "Reviewed Client Software", is written in the format of Enterprise-Managed Authorization in `modelcontextprotocol/ext-auth`, for proposal there. It covers the following:

- **Clients.** A client publisher lists its statements at the `software_statements_uri` the client's metadata document names. MCP clients send nothing new.
- **Authorization servers.** MCP authorization servers MUST pull and validate those statements. They take statement signing keys only from configured issuers, through `software_statement_jwks_uri`, and MUST NOT require registration.
- **Binding the presenter:**
  - Confidential clients authenticate with `private_key_jwt` at the token endpoint.
  - Public clients with https redirects use PKCE plus `dpop_jkt`.
  - Loopback desktop clients, and public clients at the token endpoint, are review-only.
- **Tenants and errors.** Tenant resolution follows the statement draft. A `statement_required` response carries a readable `error_description`.
- **Enterprise-Managed Authorization.** The profile composes with it on the same `jwt-bearer` request: the ID-JAG answers whether this user may use the client now, and the statement answers who reviewed the software. IDJAG-04 §4.4.1 requires the ID-JAG's `client_id` to match the authenticated client, so the ID-JAG, the request and the statement's `sub` all name the metadata document URL.
- **Facts checked.** The MCP facts it relies on were checked against the live sources:
  - the 2026-07-28 authorization spec deprecates DCR;
  - the spec's example client is public with loopback redirects;
  - Enterprise-Managed Authorization is an ID-JAG profile using `jwt-bearer` with a CIMD `client_id`.

## Statement draft changes (normative)

- **New "Pulled Statements" section.** It defines the `software_statements_uri` client metadata member, which MUST use https and returns a JSON object holding a `software_statements` array. It also says how a server fetches from it, filters and validates the results, and binds the presenter:
  - The server considers only statements whose `sub` is the document URL, that validate, whose `consumable_at` names `presentation`, and whose `cimd_digest` matches the fetched document.
  - The watermark still applies, and a statement the server does not apply never advances it.
  - A retrieval failure is never treated as a withdrawal.
  - On refresh, the server pulls again.
- **Behaviour change.** A pulled statement is usable at the authorization endpoint without PAR, because it never travels in a request. The public-client binding and review-only rules of §6.3.1 now apply there too. The profile depends on this.
- **New AS metadata.** `software_statement_pull_supported`.
- **IANA.** Registrations for `software_statements_uri` (DCR Metadata registry) and `software_statement_pull_supported` (AS Metadata registry).
- **Extension points.** The extension point that pull fills is retired. The issuance draft points to pulled statements as the way to publish an issued statement.

## Also

- **README.** Gains an "MCP Profile" entry.
- **`mcp-profile-sketch.md`.** Its open questions now point to the defined member and the drafted profile.

## For the author

- **CIMD coordination.** `software_statements_uri` is a member that CIMD documents carry, now registered by the statement draft. Raise it with the CIMD editors before -00, alongside the embedded-statement question from CIMD §4.3.
- **Length.** The statement draft is now 53 pages. idnits reports a new RAGGED_RIGHT warning, which comes from the page footers once a draft passes 50 pages and is not a content defect.

## Checks

- All drafts build after every commit.
- `git diff --check` is clean.
- The normative diff shows only the intended change: the PAR rule for authorization requests now exempts pulled statements.
- Other idnits warnings are unchanged.

pulls.title: Critique round 2026-10-08: claimable-redirect binding, configured required issuers, pull retrieval, MCP conformance
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
This PR applies the fixes from a fourth critique, run against `main` at `4d1af9f` by four cold reviewers:
- a security reviewer, covering the new mechanisms and regressions;
- a necessity-and-shape critic;
- a CIMD editor, working from CIMD-02;
- an MCP ext-auth maintainer, working from the MCP 2026-07-28 spec, the ext-auth README and Enterprise-Managed Authorization.

I checked the decisive claims against the drafts and their dependencies before applying anything:
- CIMD-02 §5.2: "MUST NOT cache error responses".
- MCP requires `Authorization: Bearer`.
- RFC 9449 §5 allows issuing a Bearer access token while DPoP-binding only the refresh token.
- MCP servers send per-resource scope challenges.
- IDJAG-04 §4.4.1 has a rule about `client_id`.

There is one commit per finding, and two commits correcting this round's own edits after review.

## Normative change to look at first

`consumable_at` now defaults to presentation only. A statement without the claim cannot be used at registration, so an issuer that wants registration use must name `registration`. Pulled statements are public, so the previous default made any published statement a bearer credential at registration.

## Statement draft

- **H1: review-only depends on claimable redirects, not the declared method.** A redirect URI is claimable if it is not https, or is https with a loopback or `localhost` host. One such URI makes the whole document review-only, whatever authentication method it declares. Registration rejects such a document on the same basis. Where reviewed software is required, a review-only client gets `unauthorized_client`; §10 and Table 1 now name this error.
- **H2: required issuers are configured per tenant and client-identifier namespace.** Before, the requirement was inferred from statements the server happened to see, so a holder could withhold one and fall back to a broader listing. The draft now states that software which can only be review-only is excluded from such a tenant.
- **H3: failed retrievals are no longer cached.** This matches CIMD-02 §5.2.
- **H4: an omitted `scope` sets no ceiling.**
- **M2: binding is pinned to the reviewed bytes.**
  - The key presented at redemption must come from the reviewed octets.
  - A refresh replacement must name the document currently served.
- **M3: a resolved withdrawal reaches open grants.**
  - A server SHOULD check status at refresh.
  - A failed re-pull fails the refresh; it never continues the grant under unreviewed policy.
  - The overclaim "ends them regardless" is removed.
- **M4: `consumable_at` defaults to presentation.** Renewal deliveries count as registration. Refresh replacements and pulled statements count as presentation.
- **M5: `software_statements_uri` retrieval is fully specified.**
  - `GET` with `Accept: application/json`, no redirects, and only a 200 response accepted.
  - Size and statement-count bounds of its own.
  - Statements from unconfigured issuers are discarded before any signature check.
  - Caching is tied to the document, conditional requests are allowed, and failures are not cached.
  - The IANA description is scoped to Client ID Metadata Documents.
  - Privacy text now covers URLs on another origin and published audiences.
- **M6: the digest fetch is defined.**
  - `Accept: application/json`, and any content coding is decoded before digesting.
  - A 304 counts only with a strong validator.
  - At runtime the server re-fetches once before treating a mismatch as a change.
  - The gap between publishing a changed document and getting a statement over it is stated.
- **M7: tenant source.** The tenant comes from the server's own means or from a validated signed assertion (for example, an ID-JAG), never from a value the client chooses.
- **M8: embedded statements.** A statement of this profile is never consumed from the document's `software_statement` member, at registration or at runtime. This follows the CIMD editor's option A.
- **M9: coherence.**
  - The definitions and §10 now account for pull.
  - The examples gain a pull example.
  - Pull gets rate limits.

## Issuance draft

- **H3:** it no longer caches failed retrievals.
- **M1:** an issuer withdraws a predecessor whenever its replacement is narrower in any way (document, `aud`, `aud_tenant`, `consumable_at`, or lifetime).
- **Abstract:** it now says statements are presented at registration or at runtime, or published to be pulled.
- **Authentication method:** the issuance draft now owns the rule that a declared method is required exactly, rather than attributing it to CIMD.

## MCP profile

- **Conformance with MCP:**
  - Bearer access tokens, with the refresh token DPoP-bound (RFC 9449 §5).
  - Documents should omit `scope` so MCP's per-resource scope challenges work.
  - The "MUST NOT require registration" rule applies only to clients admitted under this profile.
  - The false claim that no MCP server registers clients is removed.
  - The §1.1 overclaim is fixed.
  - An error mapping (`statement_required`, `unauthorized_client`, `temporarily_unavailable`) that never names the accepted reviewers.
- **Aligned with the statement draft:**
  - Non-loopback binding rules, and `private_key_jwt` with a loopback redirect is review-only.
  - Review-only display is raised to MUST NOT.
  - Tenants may come from a validated assertion.
  - Required issuers are configured per tenant.
  - Enterprise-Managed Authorization notes:
    - the `client_id` precondition;
    - both checks must pass;
    - under ID-JAG, a single tenant drives every check.
- **Process and examples:**
  - A note that references will be pinned once -00 is submitted and the profile will be proposed through the MCP SEP process.
  - CIMD is pinned to -02.
  - "Withdrawal is not a denylist."
  - HTTP examples for an authorization request and an error response.

## Normative audit

- **Reworded, none dropped.** Five requirements were reworded in the statement draft and three in the issuance draft.
- **Deliberately softened.** One new requirement is a SHOULD rather than a MUST: checking status at refresh, because no other party can observe it.
- **Length.** The statement draft is now 56 pages.

## Left for the author

- Move RFC 7591 consumption and the validity model out of the statement draft (raised by two critiques in a row).
- Drop presentation at PAR.
- Move tenant claims to an extension.
- Add issuer-discovery metadata.
- Lead the issuance draft with token exchange.
- Submit -00 before proposing the MCP profile upstream.

## Checks

- **Builds and figures:** all drafts build after every commit, and figures stay within 72 columns.
- **Hygiene:** `git diff --check` is clean, and idnits warnings are unchanged.
- **Normative diff:** the before-and-after BCP 14 diff shows only the changes above.

pulls.title: Move registration consumption into its own draft
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Moves RFC 7591 registration consumption out of the statement draft into a new companion draft, `draft-mcguinness-oauth-cimd-sw-stmt-registration` ("CIMD Software Statement Registration"). This reverses the earlier decision to keep registration in the statement draft (option A), on the author's instruction.

Registration has its own lifecycle, credential model and recovery protocol, which is why it moves. The dependency runs one way: the registration draft builds on the statement draft, and implementing the statement draft requires none of the registration machinery.

## What moved

To the registration draft, verbatim, with cross-references repointed:
- Consumption at Registration, including the document-only metadata rule, Registration Validity and Revalidation
- Statements from an Established Client
- the registration-specific parts of repeated consumption: the default of one registration per (iss, sub), never returning credentials on idempotent handling, and per-instance keys
- the registration column of the error table, the RFC 7591 error codes, and the expired-registration error reporting
- the revalidation example
- `software_statement_registration_validity_supported`
- the security sections on statements at registration, renewal authenticating the credential, registration fraud, registration enforcement bounds, and the observable retained-registration state
- the IANA entries for `registration_expires_at` (both registries) and `registration_validity_supported`, and the client-registration usage location for `temporarily_unavailable`

## What stayed, rewritten

- **Abstract and introduction.** They now lead with portable review of exact client metadata, enforced when admitting a client. A statement reaches the server presented in a request or pulled from where the client's document points, and the companion draft is named for registration.
- **Change After Review.** It moved under the statement section, since it governs runtime too.
- **Embedded-statement rule.** It is now a general rule in the statement section; the registration draft points to it.
- **Repeated consumption.** The section is renamed "Repeated Consumption of One Statement" and keeps the `iat` watermark and the establishment bounds.
- **Deployment model, errors, enforcement bounds, observable state.** Now about runtime only, with pointers to the registration draft.
- **PAR presentation.** It stays optional in the statement draft. The PAR requirement for registration renewal (§5.1) is unchanged and now lives in the registration draft.

## Elsewhere

- **Issuance and signals drafts.** Both cite the registration draft where they mean registration.
- **README.** Gains a section for the new draft and an updated description of the statement draft.
- **Sketches.** The deployment-model and SaaS sketches point at the registration draft for registration.

## Normative audit

- **Requirements.** Nothing was added or dropped. Every BCP 14 sentence of the old statement draft appears in one of the two drafts. Three were reworded only to repoint references, and the embedded-statement MUST now has one home.
- **Size.** The statement draft goes from 56 to 47 pages; the registration draft is 17 pages.

## Checks

All four drafts build, with no unresolved or uncited references. The new idnits warning is UNDEFINED_STATE for the unsubmitted registration draft.

Follow-up PRs, stacked on this one: drop the issuer-side `tenant` claim, then reorder the issuance draft around token exchange.

pulls.title: Drop the issuer-side tenant claim
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Stacked on #5: merge that first, then this one, whose base will move to `main`.

This PR drops the issuer-side `tenant` claim. Where an issuer's tenants are independently trusted reviewing authorities, it MUST issue under a distinct `iss` for each. `aud_tenant` and its enforcement rules stay.

## Why

`tenant` was an OIDC Enterprise claim that no one registers. It made every rule keyed on (`iss`, `sub`) carry a third key: `iat` uniqueness, the watermark, the registration bound, replacement matching, and renewal. A distinct `iss` per reviewing authority already separates keys, statuses, watermarks and trust configuration through RFC 8414 discovery, so the claim added a second way to do the same thing.

## Changes

- **Statement draft:**
  - The `tenant` claim definition is removed.
  - `iat` uniqueness, the watermark, refresh replacement, pulled-replacement selection and the establishment record are now keyed on `iss` and `sub` only.
  - Multi-Tenant Issuers is rewritten. The old SHOULD to issue under a distinct `iss` per tenant becomes a MUST, scoped to tenants that are independently trusted reviewing authorities.
  - The OIDC-ENTERPRISE reference, now uncited, is removed.
- **Introduction:** it now says that a tenant-scoped decision (`aud_tenant`) constrains where a review applies, and does not authorize any particular user or transaction.
- **Registration draft:** the recorded statement, replacement matching, the default bound, and rejection reasons no longer mention `tenant`.
- **Issuance draft:** renewal keeps `aud_tenant` and matches a replacement by `iss` and `sub`.

## Normative audit

**Removed:**
- the requirements specific to the `tenant` claim (carry it, opaque value, reserved values, reject an unconfigured tenant);
- `tenant` as part of the (`iss`, `sub`) keys.

**Strengthened:** the distinct-`iss` rule, from SHOULD to MUST for independently trusted reviewing authorities.

The statement draft is now 46 pages. All drafts build, with no unresolved or uncited references.

pulls.title: Lead the issuance draft with token exchange
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Stacked on #6, which is stacked on #5. Merge them in order; each base moves to `main` as the one below it merges.

This PR reorders the issuance draft so token exchange comes first, followed by the redirect flow and deferral. Both paths are kept.

## Changes

- **Abstract and introduction:** token exchange is presented first: first issuance with an initial access token, and renewal by prior statement. The redirect flow follows, for a client holding neither.
- **Protocol Overview:** it leads with token exchange and states the limit on renewal plainly:
  - Renewal by prior statement authenticates the reviewed client itself, with a key its reviewed document carries.
  - A public client cannot renew this way.
  - A publisher's backend acting for a client is not a party this specification authenticates. Issuance it authorizes on a client's behalf would need a protocol of its own.
- **Section order:** the Token Exchange Profile, including Renewal, now comes before the redirect-flow sections (authorization request, authorization response, code redemption). Every anchor is unchanged.

## Normative audit

None. The issuance draft has 126 BCP 14 sentences before and after, and none were removed or added. It builds at 39 pages with no unresolved or uncited references.

pulls.title: Editorial consolidation and tightening pass
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
An editorial consolidation and tightening pass across the four drafts, aimed at readability, scanability, and the style and idioms of published OAuth RFCs (RFC 9449, 8693, 9068, 7662, 9700, 9728, 8705).

## Size

| Draft | Body words | Pages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Statement | 13,139 → 11,907 | 44 |
| Issuance | 9,159 → 8,538 | 38 |
| Registration | 3,776 → 3,447 | 16 |
| Signals | 2,652 → 2,400 | 11 |

About 8.5% shorter overall. All four build; no unresolved citations, uncited references, or lost anchors.

## Method

Every BCP 14 sentence was recorded with its preceding sentence and paragraph lead before editing. Section editors worked from one fixed set of rules: no requirement may change; lowercase role nouns; fields named by kind; "Section N of [REF]"; actor-first requirements; conditions opening the sentence; lists for three or more parallel requirements. Two independent readers then checked every recorded requirement against the result, and a third read the family for consistency.

* Statement and signals drafts: the ordered keyword sequence is identical (135 and 31).
* Issuance: 169 → 163. Five sentences deleted as exact duplicates of a surviving requirement elsewhere in the draft, and one SHOULD folded into an existing SHOULD list.
* Registration: 37 → 35. The replacement rule's three MUSTs became one "MUST:" with a list.

## Commits

**Tightening (six commits, `c7b77a6` to `9a8bee0`).** Citation form first, then one commit per region.

**`d16e4bc` Restore requirements the tightening pass changed.** The checkers found four places where a cut changed an obligation; each is restored:

* Registration Validity: an expiry the reviewed document asserts is again a binding bound.
* Errors: the exclusion on the authorization-endpoint `statement_required` rule is back, so it does not capture review-only clients or failed pulls.
* Refusal Record: the trigger is again a statement that ceased to be acceptable before its expiry.
* Validation: "Status constrains and never relaxes" is back, as Public Clients cites it.

**`5cc90b7` Resolve contradictions the consistency read found.** These change requirement scope and are worth reviewing individually:

* `invalid_client` for an expired registration covers only a request with no replacement; a failing replacement is `statement_required`, as the registration draft says.
* Sender Constraint and Presentation Request name the public-client `dpop_jkt` binding as the alternative proof.
* A statement pulled for a keyless client at the token endpoint is review-only; a presented one is rejected.
* Same-server admission: the recorded decision must always be unexpired.
* Registration error table: the last row names a claimable redirection URI, which is what that draft rejects.
* Registration Enforcement Bounds: requests fail at the effective expiry.
* Issuance: the "issuance source" SHOULD now names the client; two unsupported citations of Deferred Processing and the DTR summary are fixed.

**`371d725` Align terminology across the drafts.** "proven key" lowercase in running text; "admission" for the act, "establishment" for the state; "governing statement" in the registration draft; the signals draft uses the statement draft's issuing and trusting authorization servers.

**`74ff281`, `f4cfe36` Editorial fixes.** The registration example authenticates with `private_key_jwt` (Section 4.1 of CIMD forbids shared-secret methods); examples note display line breaks; persuasive wording removed; a split parameter list rejoined.

## Not changed

* "The JWT payload MUST contain the following claims" still introduces some OPTIONAL entries.
* The MCP profile keeps its own Statement Issuer term.

pulls.title: Rename consumable_at to statement_uses
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Renames the `consumable_at` claim to `statement_uses`.

The claim lists the permitted uses of a software statement: `registration` and `presentation`. The old name read poorly: "at" suggests a timestamp or an endpoint, and "consumable" suggests an artifact that is used up, although a statement is reusable. `statement_uses` was chosen over the more generic `allowed_uses` because the claim is registered in the IANA JWT Claims registry, which every JWT profile shares, and the name should stay specific to software statements.

The definition now states the default directly: if the claim is absent, only `presentation` is permitted. The classification of edge cases is unchanged: a delivery renewing a registration is a use at registration, and a refresh replacement or a pulled statement is presentation.

Changes:

* Statement draft: the claim definition, the validation check, the error table row ("`statement_uses` excludes this use"), the `aud` and Sender Constraint references, and the IANA JWT Claims registration ("Permitted uses of a software statement").
* Registration and issuance drafts, the MCP profile, and two sketches: the name.

No requirement changes; the keyword sentences differ only in the name and in "use" replacing "point".

pulls.title: Split long sentences and prose semicolons in the statement draft
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
A selective clarity pass on the statement draft, taking the parts of an ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English) rewrite that remove real ambiguity and leaving the rest. The first version of this PR applied STE in full; it grew the draft 10% and replaced the IETF list idiom, so it was replaced with this one. The full version is kept on a local `ste100-full` branch for comparison.

No requirement changes.

## What changed

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sentences over 35 words | 71 | 9 |
| Semicolons joining clauses in running text | 69 | 0 |
| List-item terminators ("; and" / "; or") | 44 | 45 (kept) |
| Words | 12,272 | 12,416 (+1.2%) |
| Pages | 44 | 45 |

* Long sentences are split into two or three, keeping each condition with its keyword. The remaining long sentences are ones that must not change (the Refusal Record definition and the authorization-endpoint `statement_required` rule) or whose condition would leave its keyword if split.
* Semicolons that joined clauses in prose, definitions, and table cells are replaced with sentences.
* Unclear references ("it", "such", "that", "either") name what they mean.
* "consumer" becomes "trusting authorization server", and "fetch"/"fetcher" become "retrieve"/"retrieving party". Two headings still say "Consumer".
* IANA: two semicolons removed from our template values, and "the following value" becomes "values" (two claims are registered).

## What stays as it was

The list style (lowercase items, "; and" / "; or"), the "is rejected with X" idiom, the one-paragraph abstract, sentences that already read clearly, and word choices such as "validate `iat` and `exp`".

## Verification

* The ordered BCP 14 keyword sequence is identical (135 → 135). Fenced blocks are byte-identical, no anchors changed, citations resolve, and the draft builds.
* An independent check of all 135 recorded requirement sentences against the original found no lost or reversed requirement. It flagged two references that splits had loosened, fixed in the last commit: the Public Clients requirements now apply only to a presentation to which the redirect binding applies, and the Issuer Trust "only" rule names the required issuer.

pulls.title: Rejoin closely related clauses split by the clarity pass
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Follow-up to #10. A review of that PR found that some splits made the text harder to follow: two clauses that state one connected rule became two sentences, and the second leaned on the first. Examples:

* "Refresh never rotates the establishment's key; a client that needs a new key performs a new presentation" had become two sentences.
* "So is one pulled for a document whose redirection URIs that section does not accept" stood alone, depending entirely on the sentence before it.
* The Public Clients lead moved its conditions into a separate sentence, which needed a follow-up fix to restore their scope.

This PR restores the compact form in 85 places and keeps the 38 splits that helped.

| | Before #10 | After #10 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Words | 12,272 | 12,416 | 12,387 |
| Sentences | 646 | 768 | 681 |
| Sentences over 35 words | 71 | 9 | 41 |
| Semicolons joining clauses | 69 | 0 | 56 |

## Restored

The original semicolon, colon, or since/so clause, where the two parts state one rule: a rule and its corollary or consequence, a condition that had moved into its own sentence, a reason that had become a bare fact, or a second sentence that opened with "So", "This", "That", or "Such" and leaned on the first. The Public Clients lead is one conditioned sentence again.

## Kept from #10

* Splits that separate distinct obligations, or a requirement from its reason, where the original sentence was overloaded (for example the 56-word `aud_tenant` sentence, and the required-issuer MUST NOT with its reason after it).
* Every explicit referent: "the required issuer", "the retained `iat`", "the server's clock-skew policy", "the software" for an ambiguous "it", "the statement key set".
* Terminology: "trusting authorization server" for "consumer", "retrieve" for "fetch".
* The Error Responses sentence whose missing "is rejected" made it parse wrongly; its condition now covers both cases.
* The IANA corrections.

## One requirement fix

In Reviewed Metadata, #10 had moved the two permitted ways to obtain the reviewed document out of the MUST sentence into a plain sentence. The verifier flagged it. The MUST again names them, now with "only": "MUST obtain the Client ID Metadata Document at the statement's `sub`, only by retrieval or from octets it has already digested for that identifier, and compare its digest with `cimd_digest`."

## Verification

* The ordered BCP 14 keyword sequence is identical to the original (135). Fenced blocks and anchors are unchanged, and the draft builds.
* An independent check of all 135 requirement sentences against the original (before #10) found one changed requirement, the Reviewed Metadata item above, fixed here. Every kept split was checked for its condition and references.

pulls.title: Fix passages readers misread in a comprehension test
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Fixes from a comprehension test of the statement draft.

## The test

Six cold readers answered 20 scenario questions about what the draft requires, scored against an answer key. Three personas (an implementer new to CIMD, a literal-reading non-native English speaker, a time-pressed working-group skimmer) each read one of two versions blind: the draft before the clarity passes, and the current one. The readers were model agents playing human personas, so treat this as a proxy, not a human study.

All 120 answers were correct, and confidence was similar across versions. The useful result is where readers in both versions slowed down, reread, or had to infer. This PR fixes those passages.

## Changes

**A contradiction (4 of 6 readers).** External Retrieval said a retrieval failure means the server "MUST reject the request", and its scope includes pulled statements. Pulled Statements says a failed pull leaves the client unreviewed, rejecting only where policy requires reviewed software. External Retrieval now names the pull as the exception.

**Missing error codes (all 6 readers had to infer):**

* A token-endpoint presentation from a client whose document carries no key material: `invalid_client`, which the error definitions already give for a failed sender constraint.
* A missing statement from an issuer required for the tenant: the "Required statement absent" row (`statement_required`) now names this case.
* A document over the server's size bound: `invalid_client`. It was a retrieval failure mapped to `temporarily_unavailable`, whose definition tells the client to retry, which cannot succeed for an oversized document. **This is a choice; CIMD only says to abort.** Reverting the new table row and sentence restores the previous mapping.

**Wording readers misread:**

* Metadata Digest (5 readers): "MUST NOT compare a digest against a representation it did not itself retrieve, or store ..., or retain ..." becomes "MUST NOT compare a digest against any representation other than one it retrieved itself, stored under this section, or retained as [REGISTRATION] permits".
* Pulled Statements (3): "applies any of them, taking the latest `iat` from each issuer" becomes "keeps only the latest `iat` from each issuer and applies any one of those".
* Reviewed Metadata (3): "a bound of Section 6" becomes "the bound on establishments of Section 6", so it is not read as the `iat` floor, which maps to `statement_required`.
* References named: Refresh's "no longer does" and "as above", Change After Review's "Either way", and Error Responses' "either" and "Otherwise" (now "Apart from those two cases").

## Not changed

* **Open question: Issuer and Consumer as One Server (4 readers).** "Such a server MUST apply the conditions it would apply to a presentation" lists four checks. Readers could not tell whether presenter binding (sender constraint) also applies when the issuer admits a client on its own record. This needs an author decision.
* The `aud_tenant` definition says a server requiring a tenant-scoped decision "rejects" a statement without the claim, in lowercase. That already follows from the MUST NOT before it.

## Verification

The ordered BCP 14 keyword sequence is unchanged (135), fenced blocks and anchors are unchanged, and the draft builds (45 pages, +95 words).

pulls.title: Make the core self-contained for submission with registration
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Only the statement and registration drafts are planned for submission, so neither may rely on or cite the issuance and signals drafts. This makes the core self-contained.

## Moved into the core

* **Status Publication** (new section 3.4), from the issuance draft. Its requirements on an issuer that publishes status do not depend on how a statement is issued, and the core's validation already relies on them:
  * status on every statement from the point the issuer begins publishing;
  * a unique, never-reused index per statement;
  * Status List Tokens signed with a `jwks_uri` key, never a statement key;
  * `exp` in every Status List Token;
  * a later `iat` on each new token at a list URI;
  * withdrawing a predecessor when a narrower replacement is issued (SHOULD);
  * status never replaces lifetime.
* **`software_statement_signing_alg_values_supported`**, with its IANA registration, beside `software_statement_jwks_uri`, which the core already defines for issuers.

The moved requirement sentences are word for word, apart from "consumer" becoming "trusting authorization server" to match the core's terminology. The issuance draft's Status Publication section now points to the core.

## Citations removed

The core no longer cites the issuance or signals drafts:

* "{{ISSUANCE}} defines how a client obtains a statement" becomes "This specification does not define how a client obtains a statement."
* The `aud` definition drops the pointer to issuance's audience-narrowing rule, which applies only to that protocol.
* The rule that a request to issue a statement MUST NOT carry `software_statement` stays; its pointer to issuance's request identifiers goes.
* The privacy and Enforcement Bounds sentences drop their citations, and the Acknowledgments describe the split without one.

The registration draft drops its single citation of issuance. The signals draft now cites the core for status publication.

## README

Says which drafts are planned for submission.

## Checks

All four drafts build with no unresolved or uncited references. Registration and signals keep their requirement sentences unchanged. The core is 47 pages.

pulls.title: Require the sender constraint when admitting on the issuer's own record
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Resolves the open question from the comprehension test: when an issuer admits a client on its own recorded decision, without the statement being presented back, does presenter binding still apply? Four of six readers could not tell.

It does. The recorded decision replaces the presented statement; it does not establish who is making the request.

## Change (Issuer and Consumer as One Server)

* The lead now says the server applies the conditions it would apply to a **presented statement**, so the four listed checks are clearly checks on the decision.
* New requirement: at runtime, the request MUST meet the sender constraint of the Sender Constraint section against the reviewed document, as a presentation would. This includes the public-client binding and the review-only cases that section defines. A successful admission creates an establishment (Grant Lifecycle), so redemption and refresh bind to the proven key as for a presentation.
* At registration, the registration draft's rules apply as they do to a statement presented there. They are unchanged.
* "presents nothing" becomes "presents no statement", since the client still proves possession.

This adds one MUST to the statement draft. It is a normative clarification, not an editorial one.

Independent of #13; the two touch different sections.

pulls.title: Shorten the introduction and abstract to the usual OAuth RFC shape
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
The introduction and abstract were longer and denser than OAuth RFCs typically are (compare RFC 9126, 9449, 9068, 9728). This reshapes both. No requirement changes; the keyword sentences are identical.

## Introduction: about 1,070 → 400 words (with the protocol overview)

Four paragraphs and the overview:

1. The problem: a Client ID Metadata Document is the client's own claim, and a reviewer has no interoperable way to record a review or have it enforced elsewhere.
2. What this specification defines: a software statement profile binding the review to the document's exact octets, and admission at request time without a registration, portable across authorization servers that trust the issuer.
3. Why possession alone admits nothing: the presenter proves a key the reviewed document carries, or receives the code at a reviewed redirection URI no other application can claim.
4. Scope: what is defined and what is not (how a client obtains a statement), the relationship to the registration draft, and pointers to the deployment model and related work.

## Moved: Relationship to Other Work (new Section 8, non-normative)

* **Client Attestation:** the former introduction subsection.
* **Identity Assertions:** the former "Relationship to Identity Assertions" section. It now opens with the admission-layer paragraph and the `aud_tenant` scope sentence from the introduction, merged so they do not repeat.
* **OpenID Federation:** from the introduction.
* **Existing Software Statement Ecosystems:** the UK Open Banking and Australian Consumer Data Right paragraph, from the introduction.

The three-bullet list of presenter binding is now one sentence, since Sender Constraint has the detail. The paragraph on ceasing renewal is dropped because Enforcement Bounds already states it.

## Abstract: 160 → 121 words

The abstract keeps the problem, what the statement records, admission without registration, how the statement reaches the server, why possession alone is not enough, portability, and the registration companion. It drops mechanism detail.

pulls.title: Make withdrawal mechanism-neutral and move Token Status List to CIMD Software Statement Status
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
The statement draft required nothing of Token Status List. Even so, it defined the `status` claim's processing, the issuer's status publication rules, `INVALID`/`SUSPENDED` handling, caching and rollback, and the status-list keys in its own text, with Token Status List as a normative reference. Withdrawal is one optional concern, and other mechanisms may follow. This PR makes the core mechanism-neutral and moves the Token Status List binding into the signals draft, renamed to cover it.

## Statement draft

* **New Withdrawal section (3.4)** with the contract:
  * an issuer can end a decision before `exp`;
  * how a server learns of it is a withdrawal mechanism, none of which is required or defined here;
  * a server that learns of a withdrawal, through a mechanism or from its operator, holds a refusal record;
  * a withdrawal constrains and never relaxes, and `exp` remains the floor.
* **Validation:** a trusting authorization server MUST reject a statement for which it holds a refusal record. This replaces the Token Status List rule to reject `INVALID`.
* **Generalized to refusal records or withdrawal mechanisms:**
  * the refusal-record lifetime;
  * the refresh check;
  * the review-only refusal;
  * the same-server condition;
  * the narrower-replacement SHOULD, now for an issuer that uses a withdrawal mechanism;
  * the error-table row;
  * Enforcement Bounds.
* **Reference:** Token Status List is informative and listed as an extension point. The `status` claim stays listed as OPTIONAL; this specification does not process it.

## Status companion (was signals)

The signals draft becomes **"CIMD Software Statement Status"** (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-cimd-sw-stmt-status`). It is not planned for submission. A new Token Status List section takes the binding word for word: the `status` claim, Status Publication, Status Resolution (`INVALID`/`SUSPENDED`, caching, rollback, list keys), and the retrieval-schedule consideration. The events follow unchanged, under "Event Issuer Trust and Keys".

## Elsewhere

* Registration: a registration stops being valid under a refusal record, rather than on an `INVALID`/`SUSPENDED` status; the error row and recorded claims follow.
* Issuance: status publication points to the status draft.
* MCP profile, README, and sketches follow the rename and the neutral wording.

## Requirement accounting (statement draft)

* 10 requirement sentences moved word for word to the companion.
* 6 generalized as listed above.
* 1 new: reject a statement covered by a refusal record.
